newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian ministers head to Italy for aid talks.
newsitem.headline: Albanian ministers head to Italy for aid talks.

text.p: An Albanian government delegation will travel to Italy on Wednesday ahead of an international donors' conference on restoring order and stability in the troubled country, a government official said.

Spokesman Vladimir Prela said Prime Minister Fatos Nano and deputy Bashkim Fino would head a six-member delegation that will meet Italian ministers before the international conference, which begins in Rome on Thursday.
The Albanian government will present its aid requirements to the meeting, which is expected to clear the way for a second conference in October.

Albania is seeking international assistance to rebuild state structures that were destroyed in the months of violent unrest that followed the collapse of fraudulent pyramid investment schemes earlier this year.
"This is a preparatory conference for a high-level donors' conference in October. It will decide the priorities for the areas and types of international assistance," Prela said.

The demise of pyramid schemes sparked widespread violence in Europe's poorest state and led to the ousting of the right-leaning Democratic Party government and the resignation of president Sali Berisha. More than 1,500 people have died.
The new Socialist-led government won a parliamentary confidence vote on Tuesday for its programme to restore order and revive Albania's shattered economy.

"The main aim of the visit will be the restoration of order, stabilising the situation and institutional reforms," Prela said, adding Nano would meet Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi and then hold roundtable talks with ministers.
